decision.nextValidation: Short SDK-free macos-15-intel gate only; no additional full-build retry is included in this review.

invariantsVerified: Only subprocess.TimeoutExpired from the inventory subprocess call is caught; Darwin counter-probe exceptions, parsing failures, query non-timeout errors and KeyboardInterrupt retain their prior propagation behavior.

Inventory invocation, platform-specific fixed columns, subprocess timeout=3, at most three attempts, and at most two 0.25-second retry intervals are unchanged. Process creation and stdlib timeout cleanup are outside the communicate timeout; no strict 9.5-second wall-clock bound is asserted.
Partial output and stderr attached to TimeoutExpired are never parsed, merged into a complete inventory, or published.
Timeout samples keep RSS, CPU, their lower bounds and process count null, sampleComplete false and state unknown. No previous complete counters or membership snapshot are substituted.
The null lower-bound comparison is explicit; non-null known lower bounds retain the existing memory-limit comparison.
Public queryFailure contains only fixed operation/error classification, configured timeout seconds and measured elapsed seconds. It includes no command, arguments, raw output or exception text.
Each timeout is retained in partialSamples, including when a later complete sample recovers. The final complete sample supplies its own counters and membership.
Recovered samples with sampleAttempts greater than one enter recent monitor diagnostics. An unobserved interval resets ProgressWatch before the next progress inference.

Three failed inventory attempts remain incomplete and enter monitor-unavailable with null totals. The first-failure record, failure excerpts, existing owned cleanup and independent exact-child reap remain active.

Process selection, birth/generation verification, resource limits, cleanup signals, monitor retention limits, SDK inputs, plan, harness, pipeline and Runtime workflows are unchanged by this two-file patch.
limits: The historical helper timeout root cause is unknown. Its last complete 12-process R/S sample is preceding evidence, not proof of build health at the timeout instant.
The bounded pre-cleanup tail contains no classified records; that does not exclude compiler errors outside the retained tail. The historical compiler cause remains unknown.
The patch permits bounded recovery from a transient query timeout; persistent slowness still fails closed and no historical success is inferred.
Other query failures intentionally preserve existing fail-closed exception behavior. They are not silently converted into successful or empty samples.
No new Mac job, SDK acquisition, long build, native authentication execution, repository source modification or external write was performed by this review.
Package, full host/XUL completion and actual native authentication remain unverified by this patch review.

macGate.execution: NOT_EXECUTED for this patch; development and reviewer test environment is Linux.
requiredChecks: Run the eight targeted inventory-timeout tests and the existing real Mac process/generation/cleanup gates against this exact source. Prefer the complete 126-test suite with every real Mac gate executed and no skips.
Confirm injected transient inventory timeout followed by real Darwin ps/libproc sampling retains its timeout diagnostic and permits a normally exiting owned stage to complete.
Confirm persistent timeout remains monitor-unavailable with null totals, first-failure evidence and safe owned group cleanup/exact child reap.
Confirm actual timed-out helper termination and reap, native census behavior and existing generation/resource-limit guards without privilege changes.
macGate.requiredScope: One short SDK-free standard macos-15-intel diagnostic job, without a build or browser authentication claim.

providerVerification.method: Independent read-only GitHub Git commit API

resolvedFinding.description: A single inventory subprocess timeout escaped the existing sample retry loop and immediately stopped the owned build group. The patch now converts only that query-boundary exception to a classified incomplete sample within the existing loop.

recordedSuite.provenance: Execution recorded in supplied test log; full suite not rerun by reviewer.

reviewerAdditionalPortableCheck.method: Read-only real-stage execution with an injected first query timeout and a wrapped ProgressWatch factory; repository source unchanged. This is an ad-hoc reviewer check, not a committed reset-specific test.

targetedCasesVerified: Timeout followed by complete measurement on both Darwin and Linux dispatch paths, preserving one partial diagnostic and one retry interval.
Exactly three inventory timeouts produce three calls, two retry intervals and null unavailable fields; private exception values are absent.
PermissionError and CalledProcessError remain non-retried exceptions.
Counter-incomplete, inventory-timeout and complete observations preserve both partial classifications within one three-attempt budget.
TimeoutExpired and KeyboardInterrupt raised by the Darwin counter probe are not misclassified as inventory timeouts.
An actual timed-out query child is killed and reaped before the next sample.
Persistent timeout in an actual owned stage records monitor-unavailable, durable first failure, before/after excerpts, verified group cleanup and exact leader reap.
An actual owned stage continues to successful exit after an injected first inventory timeout followed by real inventory queries.
